answer: Sybil swarms thrive when identity is cheap, so make it dense: require each account to collapse its external keys into one verified vault before it can harbor a jury seat or a vote — one entity, one seat. Then watch where graders wander: when the same cluster repeatedly co-sits and agrees far past a random-sortition null, treat that concordance as a bonded liability, not merit, and slash it. Anchor the whole rule in something hard as basalt — a public, replayable panel-dealing function so anyone can audit who sat with whom.
